name: memory_queries
title: Likely-prompt queries for saved facts
description: Write, or list the facts that still lack, the likely-prompt queries recall matches a user's prompt against — for each fact, the prompts a user would type when that fact is what they need. Call it with {} at the end of a session that saved facts, or when bantamkit_status reports `queries: n of m facts` with n below m: it answers up to 10 facts with no queries yet (layer, name, description, a body excerpt), the writing instructions, and `remaining`. Then call it with {"facts": [{name, layer?, queries}]} to store what you wrote. Every item is checked before anything is written and the first bad one refuses the whole call — an unknown name or layer, more than 8 queries, one over 200 characters; `queries: []` removes a fact's entry. No fact file changes: queries live in a per-layer sidecar under ~/.bantamkit/queries/, keyed to the fact's content, so a fact edited later is listed as missing again. memory_save takes `queries` directly for a fact you are saving now; this tool is for facts already on disk.

layer.description: project, profile, extra:<name> or native; optional: the first layer holding the name

queries.description: Up to 8 prompts, each at most 200 characters, in the user's language and in English; [] removes the fact's entry.

facts.description: Omit to list the facts missing queries

result.description: `missing` for the list call, `written` for the store call, `error` with `reason` when refused.

facts.description: With `missing`: up to 10 {layer, name, description, body} still without queries.

remaining.description: How many facts across the readable layers still have no queries after this call.

instructions.description: With `missing`: how to write good queries.

written.description: With `written`: how many items were stored.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
